subject.name_or_desc: A lady (the querent), whose husband was a prisoner

context.question: Of her husband imprisoned — when shall he be delivered?
context.setting: Her husband was imprisoned (in a garrison, in time of war); she asked when he should be delivered, and was told she need make no friends for his delivery.

attachments.key_positions: Jupiter, lord of the seventh (significator of the lady's husband), in Cancer retrograde and in his exaltation, lately or the day before in a trine with the Sun; the Moon applying to a sextile of Saturn retrograde, then to a trine of Jupiter, with a most forcible reception
attachments.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment.

provenance.book: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II
provenance.chapter: Book II, Chap. XCVI: a lady, of her husband imprisoned, when he should be delivered (Fig. 30 in the 1852 Zadkiel edition)
provenance.version: 1647 first edition (Internet Archive scan OCR, auxiliary/christian-astrology-vol1-3_djvu.txt); wording cross-checked against the 1852 Zadkiel edition (Introduction to Astrology) and the second OCR (christian-astrology-1647-original_djvu.txt) where noted
